## Caveat

* [rustc and LLVM limits on huge generated functions](rustc-limits-on-generated-code.md) - A 36k-call generic function OOMs rustc's MIR ReferencePropagation at 13.9 GiB and a 36k-statement one takes 52 min in LLVM's scheduler; generated Rust must be chunked.

## Design

* [Arena reuse between helicity-summed read-outs](arena-reuse-cache.md) - A fill_token plus bit-compared momenta stamp on ScratchSpace lets AMP2, |M|² and event read-outs share one fill; any writer retires it; prefix sharing was measured a NO-GO.
* [Constant collection and fused scaled sums](constant-collection-and-fused-sums.md) - collect_constant_factors, fuse_scaled_sums (Op::AddScaled), pair_config_weights and real-pool folding remove single-use constant scalings; found by Zen 4 counters, timed on Emerald Rapids.
* [The egglog rewrite stage as built](egglog-rewrite-stage.md) - How the lowered AST maps onto an egglog Node datatype, the identity round trip in helas/eval/egraph.rs, the unapplied typed-sorts schema, and which rewrites equality saturation suits.
* [The helicity program: typed instruction stream, SoA arenas and the fill_arenas loop](evaluator-program-layout.md) - Binary Mul peepholed into typed Instr variants, SoA per-type arenas with 8 B tagged Const, hoisted arena slices, kernel inlining, and the fill_arenas alternatives measured dead.
* [Helicity expansion and zero-operand pruning](helicity-expansion.md) - Every helicity combination baked into one hash-consed program so each distinct current is computed once per point; liveness slots, lazy expansion, and probe-verified removal of zero operands.
* [Float reassociation in the Lorentz kernels](kernel-float-reassociation.md) - Serial accumulation chains in dot/dot4/dot_lorentz/contract* are split into two-chain or tree forms by hand; f64::algebraic_* was rejected because results then depend on the inliner.
* [Lane-batched evaluation of eval_m2](simd-lane-evaluation.md) - eval_m2 over LaneField<N>: broadcast_lanes, the lane-uniformity branch contract, the bit-identity gate, and why lanes are built but not in production.

## Design Decision

* [Arena bounds checks stay in the evaluator](bounds-checks.md) - Unchecked arena access is worth at most 3.5–5.5% today; no shipped build uses unsafe, get_unchecked lives only behind the unchecked-study feature; which safe mechanisms LLVM accepts.
* [Decay chains are sampled in-process, with no MadSpin step](decay-chains-without-madspin.md) - The decay-chain cost ladder: |M|² cost stays near its core's while unweighting efficiency falls 2.6–16× from flat decay angles; correctness and convergence need no decay-after-generation step.
* [Diagram rooting at the vertex with fewest external legs](diagram-rooting.md) - canonical_root picks the vertex with fewest attached external legs (~20% fewer post-CSE nodes); greedy rooting buys ~1% more and was rejected. Soundness rests on anchor-read convention signs.
* [Op-blocked execution order within ASAP levels](execution-order.md) - Program::build groups instructions by Instr variant inside each ASAP level: level grouping pays on every program, dispatch predictability on long ones; arena and shuffled orders lose.
* [LaneField<N> as a newtype over wide](lane-field-over-wide.md) - The SIMD lane field is a wide::f64xN newtype implementing num_traits::Float because numeric-array arithmetic would not inline; alternatives weighed, and the lane exactness contract.
* [Kernel multiply-adds go through Real::mul_add_fast](mul-add-fast.md) - Scalar and lane fields share one complex multiply-add on Real::mul_add_fast (hardware FMA or product+sum), enforced by clippy; restoring the packed complex idiom is x86-only and lost 8–9% on ARM.

## Feasibility Study

* [Compiling the helicity program ahead of time](aot-compilation-study.md) - Rendering the bytecode to Rust (inlined, outlined, MadGraph slot-array form): small programs gain up to 2×, the 2→6 loses to instruction footprint in every form.
* [E-graph DAG-cost extraction](egraph-dag-extraction.md) - egglog extracts by tree cost; the DAG extractor in egraph.rs; why sharing rewrites are NO-GO without ILP extraction, a work cost model and a ≥3-consumer demo; lowering's ±1-node hash-seed variance.
* [Tail-call-threaded dispatch (not adopted)](threaded-dispatch-study.md) - become-threaded dispatch is bit-identical but loses 1.5–11% to the match loop (geomean, by host and width); preserve_none with register arenas only ties at lanes8; archived at tag study/threaded-dispatch.
* [Helicity-summed |M|² from completeness relations](trace-form-msq-feasibility.md) - Whether a trace-form |M|² speeds integration: cost by multiplicity, the Amdahl cap, obstacles, the reconstructed per-pair and full forms timed against eval_m2, and the recommendation.

## Measurement

* [The hosts behind the performance numbers](benchmark-hosts.md) - CPU, caches, measured clock, ISA, OS and toolchain of each benchmark host (M3 Max, Emerald Rapids VM, Cascade Lake VM, Zen 4), and the M3 Max run-to-run noise floor.
* [Where integrate and sample time goes, and per-point allocations](integrate-profiles.md) - samply profiles: evaluator 50–63% of self time, PDF interpolation 14–19% on hadronic paths, allocator 6–18%; the scale-draw cost and the per-event clustering allocations hoisted since.
* [integrate thread scaling](integrate-thread-scaling.md) - Serial/parallel fit of integrate at -j 16 (Amdahl, not stalled threads), the serial floor's parts, and the digest-identical speedup measurements.
* [Integration against MadGraph: throughput and time to accuracy](integration-vs-madgraph.md) - Integrand points per CPU-second and CPU seconds to 0.1% on σ against MadEvent on M3 Max and Cascade Lake, and why cumulated_time puts an O(1) factor into every such ratio.
* [Where the interpreter's time goes, and how far each estimate reaches](interpreter-overhead-budget.md) - The fill_arenas per-address profile (M3 Max, 9bad54c), x86 counter shares and the AOT lower bound side by side: most cost is the per-value arena round trip, not dispatch.
* [Lane versus scalar per-event cost, per host](lane-throughput.md) - LaneField per-event cost against scalar (0.57/0.32/0.25× at N=2/4/8 on Emerald Rapids), best width per host (Zen 4, Emerald Rapids), transpose exonerated; ARM not yet re-measured.
* [Matrix element per point against MadGraph's MATRIX1](matrix-element-vs-madgraph.md) - ns per evaluation against MATRIX1 over 19 processes on M3 Max and Cascade Lake (geomean 0.87× on both), with the dated earlier points 1.24× (14 rows) and 0.98× it improved from.
* [Reweighting cost against MadGraph's reweight module](reweighting-cost-vs-madgraph.md) - Per event and hypothesis: MadGraph 720–800 µs (mostly Python I/O), vibegraph exact 5–14 µs, the polynomial path 100–320× cheaper; an order-of-magnitude comparison only.
* [Roofline census of the helicity evaluator](roofline-census.md) - Exact op and byte counts against measured time on Emerald Rapids at db5fd03: not byte-bound; large scalar rows reach 51–68% of the operation-mix FP-issue ceiling, lanes 25–52%; the 2→6 at lanes8 was L2-capacity bound.
* [Top-down counters on Zen 4](topdown-zen4.md) - PMU slot accounting at widths 1/4/8 on EPYC 9534: the evaluator is bounded by macro-op count and FP dependency latency, not FLOPs, memory or branches; width 1 under native gets SLP-vectorised.
* [Validation-layer and MadGraph stage timings on the M3 Max](validation-layer-timings.md) - Per-row wall times of the validation layer and MadGraph's per-stage times at 45a7d62, re-measured at 62d78e4: integrals −53.7% one row at a time, validate 691 → 391 s.

## Procedure

* [Timing validation rows and integrate runs](end-to-end-timing-protocol.md) - Pin RUST_TEST_THREADS and RAYON_NUM_THREADS for per-row times; duration_s is not a benchmark; isolated is not in-pass; same-host ratios only; per-point cost rises with acceptance.
* [Benchmarking the evaluator](microbenchmark-protocol.md) - eval_strategies (16 events per iteration, BENCH_ROWS), min over rounds, layout-noise padding, in-process A/B slicing, call and lane asm census, re-measuring lanes on a new host.
